top_signals.title: Oil price falls back as traders remain focused on Middle East conflict
top_signals.summary: International benchmark eases after soaring to $117 late last week
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Mercuria Says Rival Fears Made Baltic Keep Disputed Tanker Rate
top_signals.summary: Commodity trader Mercuria Energy Group accused the Baltic Exchange of continuing to publish the world’s benchmark oil tanker rate, despite distortions caused by the Iran war, because it feared losing business to a competitor.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Saudi Aramco Nears Signing of $10 Billion Loan with Global Banks
top_signals.summary: Saudi Arabian state-backed oil company Aramco is nearing agreement with international banks on a $10 billion loan that would bolster its finances as conflicts in the Middle East threaten crude exports.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Frank Elderson: From climate and nature risks to economic resilience and competitiveness
U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026
top_signals.summary: The U.S. refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with refinery utilization averaging more than 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998. Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.
